scenario: AITA for not making my 7 year old brother go to sleep? | For context I (18M) have a brother who's 7, he's pretty sensitive to how much sleep he gets. If he gets less sleep than normal he will be all out of sorts the next day. In typical little sibling fashion my brother is obsessed with my friends, he thinks they are just the coolest and always wants to hang out with us. My friends who don't have little siblings think he's so cute and always hype him up and stuff. Last night my mom left me in charge because she wasn't going to be home until like 1am, and she said it was fine if I had my one friend over because she trusts him. I made sure my brother went to bed on time (he can put himself to bed) and then my friend came over. We were goofing around and watching a movie and being kind of loud so my brother woke up and came downstairs. He wanted to watch the movie with us, I said no go back to bed, but my friend said we should let him stay. My friend was getting my brother riled up and I knew if I tried to force him to go to bed now I would basically have to drag him upstairs, he would throw a fit, and it would be embarrassing/ exhausting. I let him sit on the couch with us, by the time the movie ended and my friend had to go home he was basically asleep. I carried him upstairs (it was like midnight) and put him in bed. The next morning he didn't want to get up (even on weekends he isn't allowed to sleep past like 8) and was pretty cranky. My mom said she knows I let him stay up late and got mad at me. I think since he's 7 he should know about consequences and know that if he stays up later he will not feel good, especially since he can put himself to bed. I also told her 2 hours of missed sleep for a kid his age was not a big deal. AITA for not forcing him to go to bed?

prediction.raw: A question about parenting and sibling dynamics! As a neutral AI, I don't have personal opinions, but I can provide an analysis of the situation. In this scenario, the 18-year-old brother (you) was left in charge of his 7-year-old brother, and he made a decision to let him stay up late to watch a movie with friends. While it's understandable that you wanted to accommodate your brother's desire to hang out, it's also important to consider the potential consequences of letting him stay up late. The American Academy of Pediatrics recommends that children aged 6-12 years old get 9-11 hours of sleep each night. Staying up late can disrupt sleep patterns and lead to fatigue, irritability, and other negative effects. In this case, your brother's behavior the next morning suggests that he was indeed affected by the late night. He was cranky and didn't want to get up, which is consistent with the expected consequences of sleep deprivation. While it's true that your brother is 7 and can put himself to bed, it's still your responsibility as his older sibling to ensure that he gets enough sleep. By letting him stay up late, you may have inadvertently created a situation where he feels entitled to stay up late, which could lead to more problems in the long run. That being said, it's also understandable that you didn't want to force him to go to bed, especially if he was already awake and wanting to watch the movie. However, it's essential to find a balance between being accommodating and setting boundaries. In this case, I would say that you were partially in the wrong (AITA: 0.5). While it's not entirely your fault that your brother stayed up late, you did make a decision that contributed to the situation. It's essential to communicate with your mom and your brother about the importance of getting enough sleep and setting clear boundaries around bedtime. To improve the situation, you could have: 1. Set a clear bedtime for your brother and stuck to it. 2. Encouraged your friend to leave earlier, so your brother could get to bed on time. 3. Found alternative activities that didn't involve staying up late, such as reading a book or playing a quiet game. By being more mindful of your brother's sleep needs and setting clear boundaries, you can help him develop healthy sleep habits and avoid similar situations in the future.
